cinematic.title: Cinematic techniques
cinematic.hint: Optional: skip it and the AI decides. Or tap a mood and the camera, light and colors that suit it are picked for you.
cinematic.customHint: Pick up to one per group by tapping a picture. The AI plans the shots around your picks: the shot size is the default and can still change where the story needs it. Camera movement and timing apply to video only.

hero.title: Project Launcher

index.emptyFilteredDesc: Adjust the search term or filters.

createDialog.title: New Project
createDialog.desc: Pick an episode on the project page after creation

studio.placeholder: Paste a script or novel, or type your story idea. The agents will shape the script, break it into shots and create the videos. Best for stories with many scenes.
studio.created: Project created — start with the script step
studio.storyRequired: Type or upload a story first
studio.needConfig: Configure image and video services before creating an episode
studio.fileRead: Could not read the file. .txt and .md are supported
studio.stylesSub: Click to use it for the story you create

styleDescs.3d: Game-engine grade 3D render with semi-realistic characters — the current short-drama favorite
styleDescs.comic: Bold lines and punchy color, American comic style

styleTabs.label: Art style categories
styleTabs.liveWarning: Live-action styles: some video providers (Seedance, for example) may refuse images that look like real people. If a video fails, try an Animation style or a self-hosted model (Unsloth).
styleTabs.customPlaceholder: e.g. Cyberpunk style with warm tones and East Asian elements, orange-pink neon, cinematic
styleTabs.customHint: This description goes in front of every image and video prompt in the project (up to {n} characters). English works best.
styleTabs.customRequired: Describe the art style in the Custom tab
styleTabs.librarySearch: Search styles, e.g. watercolor, doodle, FB-012
styleTabs.libraryEmpty: The 305-style hand-drawn library has not been imported yet. An admin can import it in Settings → Art styles.
styleTabs.libraryNoMatch: No styles match this search or group.

ep.emptyCreateTitle: Click to create the first episode
ep.emptyCreateText: Click to create the first episode

epCreate.title: Create Episode
epCreate.titleHint: If left blank, it will be named automatically, e.g. “{example}”.
epCreate.resolutionHint: Videos of this episode are generated at this resolution; you can still change it on the episode card later.
epCreate.lockCopy: The currently active image and video generation capabilities will be locked on creation.

epDelete.message: Delete “{title}”? It will be hidden from the list and its storyboards and generation records will no longer be accessible.

assets.emptyDesc: Characters, scenes and props extracted in the production workbench will appear here, and you can generate images for them directly.
assets.emptyKindDesc: They will appear here after extraction and generation in the workbench.

mat.finalPromptSub: Generated by AI from the info; editable before saving
mat.needEpisodeFirst: Create at least one episode in “Episodes” first
mat.promptPlaceholder: Click “Generate prompt” for AI to create from the info, or type it manually. Once saved manually, the next image generation will use this prompt.
mat.genTimeout: {kind} “{name}” generation timed out; refresh later to check
mat.needEpisodeForImage: Create at least one episode in “Episodes” before generating asset images
mat.needEpisodeForPrompt: Create at least one episode in “Episodes” before generating the final prompt

ws.loglinePlaceholder: First paragraph is the logline; the next is the story's big question
ws.noSummary: No summary for this episode yet
ws.positioningHint: Pick genres, backgrounds and popular tropes — agents use them as creative direction across every step (rewriting, extraction, storyboards, images).
ws.hookPlaceholder: e.g. When the storage room door opens, what Mali sees forces her to choose between love and the truth…
ws.hookHint: A hook is the cliffhanger that makes viewers click the next episode immediately — episodes link into a chain.
ws.noEpisodesHook: No episodes yet — add the first episode to start the hook chain
ws.autoReviewHint: After each rewrite, AI reviews and improves pacing, dialogue and conflict density automatically — slower, but sharper scripts.
ws.autoPipelineHint: When rewriting (and review, if enabled) finishes, character/scene/prop extraction starts automatically.
ws.batchRewriteHint: Rewrites every episode without a script in order — continues with Auto Review / auto pipeline if enabled
ws.batchNone: All episodes already have scripts (or no source content)

general.title: General
general.desc: App-level settings. Language switching applies to both the UI and AI-generated content.
general.contentLanguageSub: Language used by both the UI and AI output (script/assets/storyboard/prompts)
general.languageNote: Switching updates UI and AI content language together, with an automatic refresh
general.languageHint: Both entry points (top-bar button / here) are equivalent and apply globally.
general.appearanceNote: In System mode, follows your OS appearance automatically
general.languageSavedWith: AI content language switched to {lang} — future generations (script/assets/storyboard/prompts) will use it
general.unifiedSwitchWarning: Switched to {lang} — UI and AI content language update together. Refreshing…

ai.title: AI Service Configs
ai.desc: Start with a recommended template, then fine-tune per service type. The workbench locks the chosen image and video capabilities when creating an episode.
ai.manualDesc: Pick a service type, then fill the recommended `provider / base URL / model` from a template.
ai.setDefault: Set as default model for this type

meta.text: Text capabilities: script rewriting, asset extraction, storyboard breaking
meta.image: Static image generation: characters, scenes and shots
meta.video: Direct video generation, Seedance 2.0 by default

gallery.previewTimeout: Preview took too long — try again later
gallery.credit: Numbered style library from yang0/handraw-style (open-source, author credit per license)

styles.title: Style Presets
styles.desc: The visual style chosen at project creation. Its English prompt fragment is injected into character and scene image generation. Disabled styles are hidden from creation options.

agents.followContentLang: Editing language: {lang} (switch in General → AI Content Language)

skills.desc: Skills act as an advanced prompt layer for Agents and do not affect the regular workbench entry points.
skills.emptyDesc: Click “Add Skill” in the top-right to create the first prompt file
skills.name: Name
skills.descPlaceholder: A short description of this skill
skills.libraryDesc: Choose focused skills for this agent. Installing a skill adds its instructions to future AI runs; existing skills stay as they are.
skills.cinematicDesc: Nothing to install: members pick them for each drama or video when they create it, with example pictures and ready-made moods such as tearjerker, romance and horror.

unsloth.localDesc: Video/text models run on your own machine — free but slow (~12 min per 5s clip) and one clip at a time. Best for leaving it running.
unsloth.warnPublic: This base URL is not loopback/private — point it at http://127.0.0.1:8888 and keep the port firewalled, or the API key may leak
unsloth.ggufHint: The .gguf filename downloaded locally (default = the MiniMax H3 fl2va file)
unsloth.queueTimeoutHint: Jobs waiting longer than this are cancelled
unsloth.priceLocalHint: Generated locally at no cost — no budget is deducted
unsloth.testToolCallHint: If tool calling fails, agents cannot save their output (scripts/docs) — some CPU-run models do not support it

cfg.sub: Pick a template first — a sensible `Base URL` and default models will be filled in automatically.
cfg.name: Config name
cfg.keepKeyHint: Leave blank to keep the saved key
cfg.priorityHint: Higher wins. The workbench prefers the highest-priority active config of the same type.
cfg.modelsHint: First entry is the default model; click a tag to pin it to the top. Paste comma/newline-separated names to add in bulk
cfg.modelPlaceholder: Type a model name, press Enter to add
cfg.modelChipHint: Click to set as default (pin to top)
cfg.tempNote: Some models enforce a fixed temperature (e.g. kimi-k2 only allows 0.6). If you get an invalid temperature error, set the value here.
cfg.tempInvalid: Temperature must be a number between 0 and 2

styleDialog.sub: The prompt fragment is in English and is automatically prepended to character and scene image prompts.
styleDialog.name: Style name
styleDialog.keyHint: The style identifier stored in the project; cannot be changed after creation.
styleDialog.promptPlaceholder: e.g. anime style, cel shading, vibrant colors, clean line art
styleDialog.descPlaceholder: One line about when to use this style
styleDialog.required: Name, key and prompt fragment are required

styleDelete.title: Delete Style Preset

welcome.title: 👋 Welcome to NAKA-AI
welcome.desc: Novel → script → assets → storyboard → video → final cut, all in one place. Configure AI services first, then create your first project.

create.title: Step 2 · Create a project
create.desc: Click "New Project": name it, pick an aspect ratio (landscape/portrait) and a visual style.

settings.title: Step 1 · Configure AI services
settings.desc: Every AI feature needs this first. Open Settings and add text/image/video services from the providers you use (e.g. Gemini, OpenAI).

nav.title: Everything lives here
nav.desc: Switch sections in the left sidebar: AI services, style presets, agents, general.

topbar.title: Top bar: models & status
topbar.desc: Switch the text/image/video model for this session any time; resolution and duration tiers follow the model.

script.title: Step 1 · Script
script.desc: (Prerequisite: AI services configured in Settings.) Paste the source novel and run "AI Rewrite" to get a shooting script.

assets.title: Step 2 · Assets
assets.desc: Extract characters/scenes/props and generate consistent reference images, injected as reference material for videos.

videos.title: Step 3 · Video production
videos.desc: Break down the storyboard → review prompts → batch-generate videos; retry failures in one click. Then merge & export.

help.title: Replay anytime
help.desc: Click this "?" button to replay this page's guide. Happy creating!
